pillar_reactions.evidence: The rep delivered a long technical version - eight primal movement patterns, linear versus nonlinear, nervous system inhibition of muscle fibre recruitment, and a reference to Pavel and 'greasing the groove' - and the prospect responded 'None. Yeah.' when asked for questions. He was already converted to the modality before the call started: 'Since I've been doing kettlebells, actually, my spine feels stronger. It's helping me to not injure myself... I'm never looking back. I'm always going to do those types of exercises.' That is agreement with the premise, not with the offer, and it meant the pillar had no persuasive work left to do.

The only pillar he responded to positively and unprompted, and the only one he offered to pay for separately. He raised it himself before it was presented - 'if you guys have a nutrition segment of this, then I would be willing to dive into that too' - responded 'Yeah, I like it' when it was delivered, and returned to it after the price objection: 'as far as getting my abs to show again, I just got to be more strict with the nutrition. You know, I'm fully aware of that. I like the idea of a simple thing to do. And for that, I'd probably pay some money too, you know, for that piece.' A standalone nutrition offer would have closed on this call.

He pushed back on the substance of the delivery mechanism, though the objection landed before the pillar was formally presented. Describing the Ben Patrick programme he said: 'it was a delayed response because I had to go through the trouble of filming it, and then I'd send it, and then I had to wait for them, and it was, for the work, I'm not sure the juice was worth the squeeze.' He then specified what would work instead: 'if we were talking like you and I, and you're like, hey, back up and do it, and you looked at it, and you gave me some instant feedback, something like that would be helpful.' When the pillar was presented as 24/7 access and video submission he said 'None. I don't have any questions', and later restated the objection as a cost: 'To send it to Trevor, I'd have to record myself.'

anchors.raw: My thing is, I just, you know, I've talked to other people, I've been through this process before, and if it's like $2,000, I'm good. If it's like, joining me. Thanks, Eight or nine, I'm out.
anchors.note: Proposed label: preemptive_self_declared_ceiling. Delivered at 00:01:00, before any discovery, any pillar, or any value construction. It is the earliest and hardest anchor in the batch and it never moved: he restated it twice more, at 'Like $2,000, $3,000, no problem. Where do I sign?' and 'for a few grand, I would do it, but five, six, it's probably just a little higher than I need to go.' Because discovery was skipped there was never any counterweight built against it.

anchors.raw: I'm a, I'm a YouTube kettlebell warrior, man. I just watch and try to learn as much tips and, and stuff... but I mean, just doing that, I've gotten some pretty good results
anchors.note: Proposed label: free_method_that_already_worked. Eighteen months to two years of free instruction that produced results he is happy with and, in his account, a stronger spine. This is the same anchor that sank the Sean Stover call in this batch and it is the more dangerous version, because here the free method solved a medical problem the prospect cares about more than aesthetics.

anchors.raw: I was doing the Ben Patrick program for a while and I was learning how to do a lot of that knees over toes stuff. Uh huh. Then I would send them videos and they would analyze it and send it back to me.
anchors.note: A directly comparable product he has already bought and used, and whose central mechanism - asynchronous video form review - he judged not worth the effort. The rep surfaced this himself with a good question and then built the entire differentiation of the pitch on that same mechanism. No price for the Ben Patrick programme was ever asked, so the reference point it set is unknown.

anchors.raw: So I sell high-ticket items. I sell $10,000 decompression packages to people. So I've worked off all that stuff.
anchors.note: Proposed label: sells_high_ticket_himself. Genuinely supportive in principle - he is not shocked by four or five figures, confirmed 'I can afford it', and later described his own $10,000 fourteen-month plan and how he justifies it to patients on effectiveness versus surgery. He handed over his own value framework and the rep never used it. The same disclosure also cut the other way: 'I've worked off all that stuff' is notice that he recognises the process and will not be moved by it.

anchors.raw: even if I found someone here locally to teach me some of these things, I know I wouldn't be paying $1,000 a month to work, you know, to work together that much
anchors.competitor: An unnamed local in-person trainer or coach in Chattanooga
anchors.note: He converted $6,000 into $1,000 a month himself and set it against local in-person instruction, which is also the delivery format he said he actually wants. The rep's answer questioned whether a local trainer would be expert enough, which raises doubt about the alternative without adding evidence for the offer.

unmet_demand.want: Real-time form correction - someone watching him move and saying 'back up and do it' with instant feedback.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme delivers form correction asynchronously by video submission, which is precisely the mechanism he had already tried on another programme and abandoned as not worth the effort. He named the alternative he wants and it is not what is being sold.

unmet_demand.want: A version of the offer at two to three thousand dollars. He asked for it in plain words: 'I don't know if you have another version like that'.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing between $199 a month and $6,000 exists, and the $199 tier was never mentioned to him at all, despite the same rep leading with it on two other calls in this batch. His question went unanswered.

unmet_demand.want: The nutrition component on its own, which he identified as his real gap and volunteered he would pay for separately.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nutrition is only sold bundled inside the six or twelve month programme. There is no standalone nutrition product, and the rep did not explore the offer even after the prospect made it twice.

unmet_demand.want: Certainty that the paid programme differs materially from the free videos he already follows - the objection he named as his fear.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No guarantee, trial, risk reversal, proof or sample was offered, and the rep opened his answer by conceding the point: 'you don't really know until you're in it'.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that loaded kettlebell progression is appropriate for someone with L5-S1 and L4-L5 herniations and a prior microdiscectomy.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The injuries were asked about once and never revisited. No clearance question, no discussion of contraindicated movements, and no description of how programming adapts to a repaired disc - despite injury prevention being his stated primary goal.
